title: SLA quotas, true-up policy, and enterprise fallback pricing experiment for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Experiment to define a pragmatic commercial and contract framework for Dedicated GPU capacity that balances enterprise SLAs, predictable reserved pricing, burst/fallback pricing, and a quarterly true-up mechanism. Goal: reduce procurement friction for large customers while protecting unit economics and keeping autoscale/burst behaviors operationally safe.
background: Customers want: (a) guaranteed baseline throughput for mission-critical flows, (b) simple burst behavior when traffic spikes, and (c) clear contractual remedies and predictable billing. Current offers (reserved GPUs + ad-hoc burst credits) create edge cases: overcommitted reserved pools, silent overage spikes, and lengthy negotiation cycles tied to legal/security questionnaire (SIG/SSQ) answers. This experiment explores a quota-first SLA coupled with a quarterly true-up and well-defined fallback-priced shared pool to simplify contracts and shorten sales cycles.
acceptance_criteria:
- Define three quota tiers (Baseline, Buffer, Surge) with clear throughput and latency SLOs for each tier.
- Produce a pricing matrix that includes reserved monthly unit price, burst price per GPU-minute, and shared-pool fallback rate.
- Draft the clause language for true-up (quarterly reconciliation) and fallback pricing to include in enterprise SOWs and the Security Questionnaire addendum.
- Run financial simulation for three representative customer profiles (steady, spiky, seasonally-bursty) and show NPV/unit economics within target bounds.
- Legal and Security sign-off on proposed SSQ language for capacity guarantees and incident reporting timelines.
proposed_options:
1) Hard-reserve + fixed burst credits: customer buys X reserved units and receives Y burst credits/month.
2) Quota-SLA + true-up: customer commits to a Baseline quota; usage above Baseline billed at burst rates and reconciled quarterly for effective committed capacity.
3) Hybrid fallback lanes: Baseline reserved, Buffer priced at discounted burst, Surge transparently routed to shared pool at a premium; automatic fallbacks with throttling rules.
(Each option includes variations for pre-pay discounts, minimum term, and escalator clauses.)
recommended_option: Hybrid fallback lanes (option 3) with a quarterly true-up. Rationale: operationally smoother (automated fallbacks), reduces latent legal negotiation by codifying fallback economics, preserves unit economics via tiered burst pricing, and gives customers predictable high-priority capacity through Baseline quota and Buffer lanes.
decision_notes: PM/Finance workshop 2026-03-05 selected Hybrid fallback as default commercial template. Key trade-offs: choosing a premium Surge rate protects economics but risks customer churn if perceived as punitive—mitigate by offering a limited free Buffer window in onboarding. Security requested explicit logging clauses and a standard audit cadence; Legal wants a short arbitration clause for billing disputes.
open_questions: What should be the default Buffer window (minutes/day) for new customers before burst rates apply?
How granular should the true-up be (per-GPU-minute vs. vCPU-equivalent)?
Can we automate contractual true-up notices via Console billing exports to reduce ops overhead?
Will Sales accept a standard premium Surge rate or require bespoke negotiation for >$1M ARR deals?
success_metrics:
- Time-to-contract for Dedicated deals decreases by 30% vs. baseline.
- Average invoice disputes for capacity billing drop to <1% of deals.
- Effective utilization of reserved Baseline increases by 8% in first 6 months due to Buffer smoothing.
- Unit token cost delta vs. on-demand remains within target +/-12%.
rollout_plan:
1) Prototype commercial template and pricing matrix (2 weeks).
2) Run financial sims with 3 customer archetypes and iterate (1 week).
3) Legal/Security review and SSQ addendum draft (1 week).
4) Pilot with 2 enterprise customers (6-8 week pilot), instrument Console for true-up reporting.
5) Collect feedback, update docs and ship as "dedicated-2026.04" draft for wider availability.
Note: Pilot customers will get explicit SLA and a 60-day opt-out clause for the pilot period.
risks_mitigations:
- Risk: Customers view Surge pricing as punitive -> Mitigation: include onboarding Buffer credits and clear burst cost visualization in Console.
- Risk: Billing reconciliation overhead -> Mitigation: build automated true-up exports and standard GL mapping with Finance.
- Risk: Security/Legal delays -> Mitigation: pre-clear SSQ language with Security and Legal and create a one-page appendix.
- Risk: Operational load on autoscale paths -> Mitigation: throttle rules and autoscale safety caps; SRE ops playbook required.
